title: Q2 2026 Private Deploy: Stability Sprint, Interop Gates, and Migration Playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Quarterly planning ticket to coordinate a focused stability sprint for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), define interop compatibility gates across runtime-1.x and orchestration layers, and author a customer migration playbook for customers moving from hosted to Private. Goal: reduce upgrade-related incidents by 60% for Q2 migrations and enable two pilot customer migrations with zero critical regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Define compatibility gate checklist covering model binary formats, quantization profiles, and kernel selection matrix
Run two end-to-end private upgrade rehearsals in staging with production-like datasets
Publish Customer Migration Playbook doc with rollback instructions, KB articles, and contact list
Instrument rollout with canary metrics (error-rate, tail-latency, token-cost delta) and alert thresholds
Get security review sign-off for KMS/HSM migration steps
comments: 2026-01-16 — Kickoff: aligned with Infra and SRE on stability sprint scope. Decided to prioritize KV cache consistency fixes and batching fallback behavior during partial upgrades.
2026-01-22 — PM sync: added explicit compatibility gate for quantization profiles after Eng raised risk with int8 mismatch in edge cases. Action: Eng to maintain a compatibility matrix in GitHub.
2026-01-28 — Design review: Console UX for migration — added a ‘preflight check’ step in the rollout wizard. DES feedback: show estimated token-cost delta pre-migration.
2026-02-03 — Risk: identified customers using custom kernels that may require vendor-specific patches. Mitigation: create a manual patch path and extend canary to these customers only.
2026-02-10 — Next steps: schedule two rehearsal windows (2026-03-10 and 2026-03-24), finalize playbook draft, and open security checklist PR.
notes: Trade-offs: an aggressive compatibility gate reduces customer regressions but increases engineering review cycles—plan to automate checks where possible.
Fallback policy: automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model variant if quantization mismatch detected during canary.
Runbook owners: SRE (oncall), Runtime Eng (upgrade tooling), Solutions Eng (customer coordination).
